newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SABRES TAKE 2-1 LEAD OVER SENATORS, FLYERS LEAD PENGUINS 3-0.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SABRES TAKE 2-1 LEAD OVER SENATORS, FLYERS LEAD PENGUINS 3-0.

text.p: Dixon Ward's goal with 19.8 seconds to play took the Buffalo Sabres to a 3-2 victory over the Ottawa Senators and a 2-1 lead in their best-of-seven Eastern Conference quarterfinal series.
Ottawa survived the loss of all-star goalie xxxxx Hasek, who sprined his knee in the second perid on an attempted save. Steve Shields came on to made 11 saves on 12 shots to pick up the win.

The Sabres applied constant pressure in the closing minutes as Michael Peca took a shot that was stopped by Ottawa goaltender Ron Tugnutt, who fell to the ice. The puck trickled out of the crease where Richard Smehlik pushed it to Ward, who lifted a shot from in close over the fallen Tugnutt for the game-winning goal.

Sergei Zholtok and Alexei Yashin scored power-play goals for the Senators, who lost for the first time all season when leading after two periods. It was the city of Ottawa's first NHL playoff game in 67 years.

In Philadelphia, "The Legion of Doom" line -- Eric Lindros, Mikael Renberg and John LeClair -- combined for three goals and seven points as the Philadelphia Flyers defeated the Pittsburgh Penguins, 5-3, to take a three games to none lead in their Eastern Conference quarterfinal best-of-seven series.

Flyers goaltender Garth Snow has justified coach Terry Murray's confidence in naming him the team's starting netminder, stopping 35 shots. In the three games, his only playoff starts, he has allowed just six goals.
Jaromir Jagr had his third and fourth goals of the series, both on the power play, to lead the Penguins offence.
Pittsburgh goaltender Ken Wregget made 48 saves and kept the Penguins in the game early by stopping 27 first-period shots.
